# MuseCell dossier · specimen s_884ed608cb

Run `run_269441e8496e` · blinded · 2026-10-31 19:41 UTC · models: scientist muse-spark-1.3, microscopist muse-spark-1.3, reviewer muse-wonder-1.0, segmentation classical (scikit-image), provider meta, atlas ResNet50 (ImageNet) + TVN, agent v5

**Question.** Which mechanism-of-action class explains this compound's phenotype in MCF-7 cells?

## Experiments (4 of 4 wells)

| e2 | 1 | 1 | 364 | nuc_form_factor z=-38.5; nuc_solidity z=-35.7; act_glcm_contrast z=+21.6 |

- after step 12: Protein synthesis 0.75, Aurora kinase inhibitors 0.10, Microtubule stabilizers 0.07, Eg5 inhibitors 0.05, Microtubule destabilizers 0.03

## Conclusion

**Protein synthesis** (stated probability 0.78); key evidence e9, e2, e7, e8, e5.

Why: Unanimous 4/4 NSC for one class with large similarity gap; reproducible profile.

Next experiment if this were a real lab: Nascent translation OPP-puromycin incorporation assay with washout plus phospho-H3/cytokinesis live imaging, using reference controls of the leading class and of the Aurora-inhibitor class to resolve the microscopist dissent.

## PI review

Verdict: approve.

Protocol call is decisive and consistent with the analysis.

## Unblinding

Compound: **emetine** (PubChem CID [10219](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/10219))

Identity check: name and BBBC021 structure agree

ChEMBL mechanisms: no curated mechanism in ChEMBL

## Verdict (computed by code)

Correct: the call was **Protein synthesis**, BBBC021 annotates **Protein synthesis**.

The final call is the nearest-neighbour vote over the 4 wells the agent chose (4/4). The Scientist's own call was **Protein synthesis** (agrees; right).

## Reflection

The correct Protein synthesis call was driven by reproducible quantitative morphology across all four acquired wells (0.3, 1, 3, 10 uM): extreme negative nuc_form_factor z -33 to -48 and nuc_solidity z -33 to -57 with increased actin texture act_glcm_contrast z +21 to +28. The compare_to_reference_atlas NSC vote was unanimous 4/4 for Protein synthesis with high per-well similarities 0.781-0.813, which correctly outweighed a single dissenting visual read.

What misled was the describe_phenotype read on 4 fields suggesting Aurora kinase inhibitors with lower density vs DMSO, which forced retention of Aurora, Microtubule stabilizer and Eg5 alternatives. The dose_response checks chosen did not resolve this: frac_multinucleate_proxy rho=-0.20 p=0.8 and cell_count rho=0.00 p=1 were flat despite 414 to 210 cells from low to high dose, likely because the proxy and 4-well sampling were underpowered for trend detection.

The acquisition choice to survey 1 uM then 10 uM first and then fill 0.3 and 3 uM established continuity but lacked a very low-dose DMSO-proximal anchor and same-dose replicates, so onset and cell-loss dose dependence could not be quantified well. In retrospect the quantitative NSC replication should have been trusted earlier over the visual Aurora impression.

What was right:
- Unanimous 4/4 NSC vote for Protein synthesis across 0.3, 1, 3, 10 uM with similarities 0.781-0.813 was correct for emetine
- Extreme nuclear irregularity (nuc_solidity z -33 to -57, nuc_form_factor z -33 to -48) plus high actin texture (act_glcm_contrast z +21 to +28) reproduced in all 4 wells
- Downweighting microscopist Aurora call from 0.20 to 0.10 while keeping mitotic alternatives as minor hypotheses appropriately reflected the similarity gap

What was wrong or missed:
- describe_phenotype suggestion of Aurora kinase inhibitors on 4 fields was incorrect and caused hypothesis split
- dose_response of frac_multinucleate_proxy (rho=-0.20, p=0.8) and cell_count (rho=0.00, p=1) were uninformative and failed to test Aurora vs protein synthesis despite visual lower density
- Acquisition of only 4 wells at 0.3-10 uM without a low-dose anchor or replicates limited assessment of phenotypic onset and cell-count trend

Proposed next experiment: OPP-puromycin nascent translation incorporation assay with washout plus phospho-H3 staining and live cytokinesis imaging, run with protein-synthesis and Aurora-inhibitor reference controls to confirm translation block and formally rule out the microscopist Aurora hypothesis.

## Citations

Citations verified: 2/2

- PMID [42539200](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42539200/): Structural basis for emetine inhibition of ribosome translocation in Toxoplasma gondii. *bioRxiv* (2026) — Emetine inhibits ribosome translocation, supporting a protein synthesis mechanism.
- PMID [9858605](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9858605/): Ribosomal protein S14 of Saccharomyces cerevisiae regulates its expression by binding to RPS14B pre-mRNA and to 18S rRNA. *Mol Cell Biol* (1999) — Regulation of ribosomal protein S14 via binding to pre-mRNA and 18S rRNA illustrates core ribosomal biology.
